name: Factor 55
about:
Factor 55 is based in Boise, Idaho. The company began as an engineering design firm whose staff brought extensive experience from the aerospace, defense, and semiconductor sectors, applying that rigor to a shared passion for off-road vehicle recovery.

Factor 55 designs and manufactures a line of recovery hardware including winch-line shackle mounts (UltraHook, FlatLink, ProLink), vehicle recovery kits (Owyhee, Sawtooth, Borah, Baja), kinetic recovery ropes, and a range of rigging accessories. Products are developed in-house using 3D CAD and Cosmos finite-element analysis, then validated through destructive testing at an instrumented test facility. Components are precision CNC-machined from 6000- and 7000-series aluminum alloys and 6Al-4V titanium.

The gear serves recreational off-road drivers (Jeep, truck, SUV), powersports users (UTV, ATV), and military/industrial customers. Example product families include the UltraHook XTV for side-by-sides, the FlatLink MultiMount for winch mounting, and the HD Recovery Kit Teton for heavy-duty trucks.

The company differentiates itself through its Closed System Winching™ methodology, which replaces traditional hooks with closed-link hardware to eliminate latch failure.

name: Factory Connection
old_description: Factory Connection specializes in providing the latest fashion apparel for customers in small to medium size markets.
about:
Factory Connection is headquartered in Prattville, Alabama. The company was founded in 1976 in Guntersville, Alabama, by Terry Scott and Kenny Littleton as a single 1,000-square-foot store. It remains family-owned and is now led by President and CEO Steve Williams alongside a team of executive managers, merchandisers, buyers, and regional and store personnel.

The retailer operates more than 200 stores across 16 states, encompassing over one million square feet of retail space. A state-of-the-art distribution center at the Guntersville corporate headquarters supports the network, enabling frequent shipment of new merchandise — often from limited-quantity purchases. Factory Connection buys from fashion manufacturers to offer brand-name and specialty-store apparel for juniors, misses, plus, men’s, accessories, shoes, and home décor at prices 25% to 70% below regular retail.

The chain serves consumers in small to medium-sized markets throughout Alabama, Arkansas, Georgia, Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, Ohio, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, and West Virginia, with additional expansion states identified. Its customer base includes shoppers seeking affordable, current fashion in communities not typically served by large boutiques or department stores.

Factory Connection emphasizes its innovative buying process and strong relationships with major manufacturers as the foundation for making great fashion brands available and affordable for everyone. The company’s mission has centered on bringing the latest styles to smaller towns for more than 40 years.

about:
Fairhaven Furniture operates in New Haven, Connecticut, where it has been family-owned for two generations. The founding year and the names of the original founders are not disclosed in public materials.

The company functions as a furniture retailer, carrying brands such as Stressless and Stickley alongside other lines sourced from craftspeople in the United States, Scandinavia, and Italy. Its showroom covers living, dining, bedroom, and office categories, and it operates an outlet section for discounted floor models. Services include complimentary interior design consultation for residential projects, and interest-free financing for up to 12 months. No figures for facility size, headcount, or annual sales volume are published.

Fairhaven Furniture serves residential customers, including homeowners furnishing a single room or an entire house. The design service is positioned for both partial refreshes and whole-home projects. The brand mix emphasizes durability and craftsmanship, targeting buyers who prioritize long-lasting pieces over disposable furniture.

The retailer differentiates itself by describing the business as 'a furniture store with a soul,' highlighting a curated selection of well-made goods from domestic and international makers rather than mass-market inventory. This focus on longevity and design integrity is presented as the core reason for the company's existence.

name: Falcon Fabricators Nashville
old_description: Originally founded as KFC Manufacturing, we have a 50,000 square foot facility, with state of the art fabrication equipment, and is NSF compliant.
about:
Falcon Fabricators Nashville operates from a 50,000-square-foot facility in Nashville, Tennessee. The company traces its roots to KFC Manufacturing and has spent over four decades in the food-service replacement-parts business. The plant is NSF compliant and houses a range of modern fabrication equipment.

The shop specializes in precision sheet metal work, offering laser cutting, plasma cutting, CNC punching, CNC press braking, and TIG, MIG, arc, and spot welding, backed by an experienced finishing department. Core products include 304-grade stainless-steel work tables, three- and four-compartment sinks, dish tables, sneeze guards, counter tops, rotary marinators, holding bins, and corn cookers. The company also fabricates custom metal parts for virtually any application.

Primary customers are food-service operators and restaurants, but the custom fabrication side serves businesses of all types. Falcon stocks replacement parts for brands such as Ayrking, Delfield, FryMaster, Henny Penny, Pitco, and Quality, and carries equipment like the CCF-16 shortening filtration machine, rotary meat marinators, and drop-in and counter-top corn cookers. In-stock parts ordered before noon ship the same day, with next-day and second-day air options.

The company emphasizes durability, dependability, and affordability, positioning its combination of in-house fabrication and a large parts inventory as a differentiator. NSF compliance and same-day shipping on stocked items are cited as key advantages.

name: Falcon Packaging - Iowa
old_description: The Falcon Webstore has been closed, items available for pickup at our Ohio, Georgia, and Iowa Distribution Centers
about:
Falcon Packaging operates its Iowa distribution center from Ames, serving as one of several strategically located hubs for egg packaging products. The company also maintains distribution centers in Ohio, Georgia, and a newly added warehouse in York, Pennsylvania.

The company provides custom egg packaging, including printed egg boxes and empty egg cartons, and runs a just-in-time distribution model supported by more than 220,000 square feet of total warehouse space. Its services encompass warehousing, inventory management, and direct delivery to egg producers of all sizes.

Falcon Packaging works with both large and small egg producers, supplying foam, plastic, and molded pulp cartons with an emphasis on recycled paper pulp as an eco-friendly option. The company also positions itself as a resource for egg safety information.

The business was built around a just-in-time servicing model designed to eliminate the hassles and costs of customers maintaining their own storage facilities, while ensuring timely delivery of packaging solutions from its network of regional warehouses.

name: Falcon Sheet Metal
old_description: Falcon Sheet Metal was founded by Willard Peck and his wife, Ramona, in 1979.
about:
Falcon Sheet Metal was founded in 1979 by Willard Peck and his wife Ramona in Salt Lake City, Utah. The company, named after the falcon for its speed and precision, began in a small rented space and has since moved three times, now operating from its own 22,000-square-foot facility in North Salt Lake. Current owners are Riley Landsaw and Charlene Barton.

The shop provides sheet metal fabrication services including laser cutting, welding, machining, forming, punching, shearing, countersinking, tapping, brushing, and deburring. It also coordinates subcontracted finishing such as plating, powder coating, and painting. The 22,000-square-foot plant houses equipment for these processes, though specific machine models are not disclosed.

Falcon serves industrial customers such as Automated Technology, as noted in a testimonial from Janet Curl. The company works with businesses requiring precision sheet metal parts, though specific industry sectors are not detailed in public materials.

The founders chose the falcon as a symbol of speed and precision, and the company emphasizes an honest approach, stating they will tell a customer if they are not the right fit for a job. ISO certification underscores a commitment to quality management.

name: Fall River Apparel Mfg. Inc.
old_description: Fall River Apparel - Fabric cutting, sewing, stitching & Warehousing
about:
Fall River Apparel Mfg. Inc. operates from Fall River, Massachusetts, in the southeastern part of the state. The company has been in the garment manufacturing industry for over 30 years, growing from a custom maker of specialty items into a large production facility. No founding year or founders are disclosed, and ownership structure is not specified.

The facility provides a full range of in-house services: fabric cutting using Gerber computerized cutters and Niebuhr cradle-feed spreading machines, contract sewing and stitching on modern equipment, pattern marking and grading via Gerber Accumark, and warehousing with inventory management through QuickBooks Enterprise and Lightspeed. It handles sample runs of fewer than 100 pieces up to large production volumes, and offers pick, pack, and ship fulfillment for online retail. At its peak the plant employed more than 100 people; current headcount is not published.

The company serves the apparel and sewn-products sector, including outerwear, home accessories, bedding, fleece, and medical products. Historical customers included well-known catalog and retail brands; current work focuses on contract cutting and sewing for outerwear, home accessories, and specialty items, plus warehousing and direct-to-consumer shipping for e-commerce clients.

Fall River Apparel emphasizes that all operations remain under one roof, giving it complete control over quality and turnaround. It markets itself as a Made-in-USA single-source partner with no minimum-order restrictions, capable of adapting processes and acquiring new machinery for custom projects.

name: Fargo Apparel
about:
Fargo Apparel is based in Fargo, North Dakota. Public records do not disclose the company's founding date, ownership model, or the names of its founders.

The business runs a custom decoration shop offering three primary processes: screen printing, laser engraving, and embroidery. Its product catalog spans screen‑printed apparel — including t‑shirts, hoodies, team jerseys, polo shirts, and mittens — as well as laser‑engraved drinkware, leather mittens, and other gift items. The company also produces promotional merchandise, flags, banners, and recognition awards such as medals and trophies. In addition to its own stock, Fargo Apparel will print or engrave on items supplied by the customer. The shop markets its services under the slogan "Custom Products Made Easy" and emphasizes variety with the tagline "More Than Just Shirts!".

The client base appears to include sports teams, corporate buyers of promotional goods, and individuals seeking personalized gifts. One testimonial on the company's site references an order for "Nolan's Crew t‑shirts," indicating work with organized groups. The range of products — from team uniforms to engraved awards — suggests the shop serves both organizational and retail‑oriented demand.

name: Fashion Tech Kansas City
about:
Fashion Tech Kansas City operates from Kansas City, Missouri, and was founded in 2010 by Laura Treas, who serves as founder and owner. Treas brought more than 16 years of experience in small-batch manufacturing and sewist training to the venture, which began as a way to help independent designers and inventors bring sewn products to market. The company later added the Artisan Small Batch Academy to address a shortage of skilled stitchers and to teach manufacturing-style sewing.

The shop provides end-to-end product development and no-minimum production for sewn goods. Services include prototyping, pattern making, sample creation, tech packs, grading, and materials sourcing, all handled in-house. A team of stitchers runs a full suite of machines capable of producing items ranging from lingerie to complex sewn inventions. The company also offers consulting and training for businesses that want to establish their own in-house sewing operations.

Clients are primarily independent designers, startups, and established brands seeking small-batch apparel and sewn-product manufacturing. The company has worked on projects spanning lingerie, general sewn products, and product inventions, and it supports customers through design development, budgeting, and production workflow setup.

Treas started the business after identifying a gap for designers who needed technical guidance and flexible manufacturing without high minimums. The operation emphasizes educating clients throughout the process, conserving raw materials, and delivering professionally manufactured products at high quality.

name: Fast Flashings
old_description: We are doing some maintenance on our site. It won't take long, we promise. Come back and visit us again in a few days. Thank you for your patience!
about:
Fast Flashings LLC was founded in June 2003 by Ian McGlynn in Kirkland, Washington. McGlynn, who had operated McGlynn Plastering Inc. from 1980 to 2005, started the company after experiencing delays and unreliable service from sheet metal suppliers on construction sites. The business began with a goal of providing made-to-order sheet metal products quickly and accurately.

The company produces custom sheet metal components including flashings, coping caps, chimney chase covers, door pans, deck saddles, siding vents, exhaust hoods, collector boxes, and sill pans. All products are made to order using advanced equipment and proven fabrication techniques. The company operates from three locations in Seattle, Kirkland, and Everett, serving Western Washington.

Fast Flashings serves homeowners, contractors, architects, and commercial builders throughout Western Washington. Its products are used in residential and commercial construction and roofing projects. Examples include custom Z flashing for a job needed before rain, and various roofing accessories for contractors.

The company differentiates itself with fast turnaround times, including overnight options, consistent workmanship, and local accessibility for pickup or delivery. It was started to address the problem of slow turnaround and unreliable service in the sheet metal industry.
